transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 mins
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Head of Platform - Nebula), Markus Lee (CTO), Priya Raman (SRE), Devon Ortiz (Product)

00:00 Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Lena, AE at Redwood. Diego is our SE, he'll do most of the technical bits.
00:08 Aisha: Thanks, Lena. We are evaluating Redwood for the inference layer for our claims automation — reliability is the top priority.
00:13 Markus: Hi all. We run a multi-region setup today and we need to understand failover policies and what happens during incidents.
00:19 Diego: Great, appreciate the context. can you share a little about current architecture and what your availability targets are?
00:26 Priya: Sure. We run services in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Critical paths need p99 under 500ms for text-generation responses, p95 under 200ms. We also have a 99.95% uptime target across the feature.
00:38 Lena: Ok, good. Are you expecting hosted Redwood or Dedicated / Private?
00:42 Aisha: We're evaluating all three. For production we like Dedicated for isolation but hosted is interesting if you can meet latency and incident guarantees. Private is on the table for compliance.
00:51 Diego: Understood. Let's talk about incident tolerance - we have a couple of levers. first is multi-region routing with health-check based routing and automatic fallback to secondary region. second is model fallbacks — e.g., lower-cost or smaller model variants that are compatible with your prompts.
01:06 Markus: How fast is the region failover? dns TTLs can be slow and clients sometimes cache.
01:12 Diego: Yeah so we do active-active in many cases; for hosted we run cross-region routing at the edge and can fail requests to another region within seconds. DNS is not the mechanism for our internal routing for sticky sessions — we use edge routing and our control plane can re-route to healthy endpoints. If you use Dedicated within your VPC, we can do either an active-active with regional endpoints or active-passive with failover.
01:33 Priya: But what about state — we have session affinity and KV cache (we call it KV cache but in some transcripts I see kv cash haha). If a request needs the KV cache from us-east, will rerouting to eu-west break the context?
01:44 Diego: Good question. for stateful sessions we recommend sticky routing or ensuring KV cache is replicated or using prefix caching that is compatible across regions. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and you can choose a cache policy — replicate hot keys or degrade gracefully by warming cache on failover. There is some warm-up time; typical warm-up adds 50-200ms depending on sequence sizes.
01:59 Lena: We should note that fallbacks can be multi-layered: 1) region fallback, 2) model fallback to a smaller quantized model variant, 3) throttling and queued responses with user messaging.
02:13 Markus: Model fallback concerns me because output quality may change. How do you manage quality/regression?
02:18 Diego: We do model profiling and recommend a fallback family with known degradation characteristics. clients can pin quality-critical routes to a primary model and non-critical ones to fallback. We also integrate evals so you can monitor quality delta when a fallback happens, and alert if the delta exceeds thresholds.
02:33 Aisha: On SLAs, do you offer region-specific SLAs for hosted? We have customers on european data residency and need a guarantee.
02:40 Lena: For hosted API we have region-aware SLAs and an enterprise SLA add-on — Dedicated offers stronger, contract-backed SLAs and Private can be negotiated as part of onboarding. We can share the SLA doc.
02:50 Devon: When you say "region-aware SLAs", is that per-region uptime, or global?
02:54 Lena: Per-region; if you choose to run only in eu-west-1 with Hosted, the SLA applies to that region. If active-active across two regions, you can agree to a higher composite SLA but it needs configuration to handle split-brain and replication.
03:08 Priya: For incident runbooks — what does Redwood provide vs what we need to own?
03:12 Diego: We provide a runbook for common incidents: region outage, degraded kernel performance, OOMs on GPUs, and model rollout regressions. The runbook includes detection hooks, automated fallback configuration, and recommended escalation steps. We'll share the runbook and a test harness to simulate failures.
03:28 Markus: Is the failover automatic or manual? can we set thresholds?
03:31 Diego: Yes, fully configurable. By default we'll failover automatically after X consecutive health-check failures or certain latency thresholds. You can set the sensitivity (conservative vs aggressive) and choose auto vs manual.
03:41 Aisha: What about cost during failover? If you route to another region and spin up capacity, we worry about surprise costs.
03:48 Lena: Good point — Dedicated has reserved capacity and burst policies that you can configure to limit unexpected spend. For Hosted we have burst capacity but we can set budget alerts and caps. Redwood Optimize can also recommend quantization or batching changes to lower unit cost during failover.
03:59 Priya: Do you support pre-warmed standby capacity in a secondary region?
04:03 Diego: Yes; customers can reserve warm pools in secondary regions. Warm pools reduce cold-starts and keep KV caches warm. Tradeoff is cost vs faster failover.
04:13 Devon: Our legal team will want the audit logs and SSO/SAML proof in order to sign.
04:17 Lena: We'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs plus details on audit logs and KMS integration for encryption at rest. For Private deployments we support HSM/KMS using your key material.
04:27 Markus: Any known customers running cross-region active-active?
04:30 Diego: A few financial customers run active-active with geo-routing. we can anonymize benchmarks but I've got a benchmark sheet that shows p95/p99 numbers per region and failure simulations.
04:41 Aisha: Could you also show an example of model fallback path? like primary -> smaller quantized -> produce degraded answer.
04:46 Diego: Sure. Example: primary is rdx-13b-fp16, fallback rdx-6b-4bit. We measured latency drop from 280ms to 120ms and quality delta approx 6% on our eval sets. We can tune the family.
04:59 Markus: How do you handle request routing for multi-tenant apps? We want strict tenant isolation and per-tenant failover policies.
05:06 Diego: We support per-route and per-tenant policies; you can specify route-level failover (region, model family, fallback order). RBAC and per-tenant quotas are exposed in Console.
05:18 Priya: Also interested in observability during incidents — will we get request-level traces and token-level cost breakdown for debug?
05:23 Lena: Yes, Console includes token-level cost, per-route latency breakdowns, traces and error analysis. For Dedicated we can stream traces to your tracing system.
05:32 Devon: Any caveats around KV cache consistency across regions?
05:36 Diego: If you require strict consistency, you'd typically use a replicated store you control and route to the region owning the canonical state, or use Private deployment where you can deploy your KV sync layer. Redwood's prefix/KV cache is eventual and optimized for latency.
05:47 Aisha: Ok this is helpful. Could you outline a proposed pilot?
05:51 Lena: Yes - propose a 4-week pilot: week 0-1 provision a Dedicated cluster in eu-west-1 (or Hosted in EU region) with a small warm pool, configure canary route, and run baseline benchmarks. week 2 simulate regional outage and run failover tests with test harness. week 3 tune fallback policies and run load tests. week 4 review results and decide next steps.
06:12 Markus: That timeline works for us, we can commit to providing traffic profiles.
06:16 Priya: we'll also need the runbook and test harness to run internal chaos tests.
06:21 Diego: We'll send the harness and a short doc on running the failover scenarios; it includes scripts to simulate node drains, regional blackholes, and model rollback.
06:32 Aisha: Any limitations around function/tool calling or streaming during failover?
06:36 Diego: Tool calling and streaming are supported; streaming may incur slight delays during fallback if the model changes families because of tokenization differences and cold cache. We recommend graceful client fallback UI to handle transient stalls.
06:50 Lena: Ok we have a set of action items and next steps. Before we close, any other concerns?
06:56 Markus: Just want to confirm contractual SLA numbers for Dedicated — can you include 99.99% and remediation credits?
07:01 Lena: Yes, Dedicated enterprise contracts can include 99.99% with credits. I'll surface sample contract language.
07:07 Devon: Great. We'll review the SOC2 materials and loop in security.
07:10 Aisha: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the runbook and pricing.
07:14 Lena: Thanks all, we'll follow up.

End of meeting notes.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels mostly correct; occasional mis-heard words ("KV cash"), filler words, and truncated sentences present.
